readout_other: Goalkeeper Game: dependence of persist-with-prediction behaviour on recent paired-transition history (experience-based and inference-based learning)
direction_notes: Hippocampal TUS reduced both experience-based and inference-based learning compared with white matter control, abolishing structure-based inference; preference learning was unaffected.
safety_notes: Post-TUS questionnaire at session end and 24 h later; k-Plan simulations gave MI below 1.9 and thermal dose not above 0.25 CEM43.

exposures.label: Bilateral hippocampus theta-burst TUS (white matter control site not listed as exposure)

device.model: DPX-500-4CH transducer driven by Neurofus PRO TPO

timing.protocol_description: Theta-burst patterned TUS: 20 ms pulses every 200 ms (5 Hz), 10% duty cycle, 80 s total (400 pulses) per hemisphere, delivered sequentially to left then right hippocampus (or the white matter control site) in one session, before the Goalkeeper Game. White matter control free-field intensity was individualised between 55 and 75 W/cm2 to match the hippocampal in situ intensity.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Three of these 23 invited participants dropped out after the first TUS session, leaving a final sample of 20 valid participants (11 female) aged between 19 and 33 years (age mean ± SD = 25.4 ± 4.6), who completed both experimental sessions.

flags.reason: 5 Hz stated in Results as theta-burst (5 Hz, 20-ms pulses every 200 ms); the Methods give pulse repetition interval 200 ms.
Paper calls the protocol theta-burst patterned TUS, but it is a single 5 Hz train of 20 ms pulses, with no nested burst structure.
K-Plan simulation, approximately 5 W/cm2 on average across participants (min 3 W/cm2 required for inclusion); value read from text, spread in a figure only.
75 W/cm2 is for hippocampal stimulation; the white matter control used 55 to 75 W/cm2.
TPO named, so neurofus; transducer is the four-element DPX-500-4CH.
Control is real ultrasound to a hippocampus-unrelated white matter site, intensity-matched in situ; no inactive-transducer sham.
Session order was counterbalanced; randomisation not stated.
TUS to hippocampus disrupted structure-based inference relative to white matter control; authors suggest noise induction rather than clear excitation or inhibition.
A post-TUS questionnaire was given (immediately and at 24 h) but its results are not reported in the main text.
No auditory control or discussion of auditory confounds found.

provenance.notes: Experiments 1 (fMRI, n=36) and 3 (behavioural, n=40) involved no ultrasound; only Experiment 2 is recorded.
